name: Common Sunflower

facts.how: Seeds roasted; buds steamed like artichoke

caution: Straightforward and safe; harvest from ground away from sprayed roadsides. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Wild sunflowers are smaller than the crop but the seeds are the same food. Cut heads as the backs yellow and the seeds firm up; dry them before shelling.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Roast the shelled seeds for snacking, or steam the unopened green buds and eat the base like a tiny artichoke.
